items.t: Air suspension strut leaks and the car sags
items.note: Owners report about $1,700 per strut and up to $8,500 for a dealer pair. Converting to conventional struts costs about $1,500.

items.t: Brake pedal sinks and braking feels weak
items.note: Check first: Hyundai extended HECU coverage to 15 years/unlimited miles on 2011-2012 Equus, so it may cost you nothing. Out of coverage, the part is dealer-only (Hyundai Parts Deal lists $1,933-$3,203 depending on engine; confirm by VIN). No Equus labor time was found, so hours are backed out of RepairPal general ABS module labor of $161-$237. Owners were quoted about $2,800-$3,000 total.

items.t: ABS module can leak inside and catch fire (recall)

items.job: Replace wiper motor cover and seal
items.note: Hyundai also extended the wiper motor warranty to 10 years/100,000 miles on 2011-2013 Equus.

items.t: Brake lights may not come on (recall)
Engine shuts off or hesitates while driving
items.job: Diagnose stalling and loss of power
items.note: Diagnosis only: the cause varies from car to car, so the repair cost depends on what the shop finds. YourMechanic lists a stalling inspection for the Equus at $95-$115.

items.job: Replace shift solenoids or transmission electronic module
items.note: Hyundai's bulletins call for this before replacing the transmission. A full replacement costs far more.

Based on KBB, since no parts-plus-labor source was found: a 2014 Equus dealer replacement is $5,227-$5,619 total ($3,925-$4,209 parts). Labor hours are backed out of KBB's $1,302-$1,410 labor charge. Ask whether Hyundai's powertrain warranty still covers your car first.

items.t: Headlights and turn signals cut out
items.note: Diagnosis only: dealers often cannot reproduce this, so the repair depends on what the shop finds. YourMechanic lists an Equus electrical inspection at $95-$115.

items.t: Active headrest pops up or cracks
items.note: Parts only: the OEM front headrest for the 2014-2015 Equus is about $1,137 sale to $1,544 list (confirm fit by VIN). No published labor time was found, so labor is not included. Ask the dealer whether Hyundai will cover it.

items.t: Airbag light from a failed clock spring
items.note: Check first: Hyundai extended clock spring coverage to 15 years/unlimited miles; confirm with your VIN. Out of coverage, the OEM clock spring (93490-3N000) is about $357 sale to $506 list. Labor is based on a Hyundai clock spring guide (about 2 hours, written for the Elantra). RepairPal lists $728-$785 total for the related Genesis.

items.t: Car pulls or alignment won't stay in spec
items.note: Ask the shop to follow Hyundai tracking bulletin TSB-11-SS-004 if a normal alignment does not fix the pull.

items.t: Leather dashboard cover shrinking or lifting
items.note: A dealer quoted about $4,500 because the windshield and dash must come out.
An owner paid $1,350 at an independent shop for a taillight; a dealer quoted $1,800.
Diagnosis only: parts depend on what is found.
